security_audit.summary: All 89 static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. The static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, illustrative HTTP calls, and environment variable examples. A separate medium semantic issue remains because broad API logging guidance lacks explicit redaction requirements.

remediation.suggestion: Require redaction of Authorization headers, API keys, tokens, personal data, request bodies with sensitive fields, and payment data before logging.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Data Logging Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends logging API interactions and failed requests with context. Without explicit redaction guidance, logs may capture tokens, personal data, or payment details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The logging guidance is explicit, and the same skill includes authentication headers and payment, email, and SMS examples. The risk depends on user implementation, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: API integrations often fail when authentication, retries, and rate limits are added late. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design secure clients and webhook flows.
actual_capabilities: Shows API key and OAuth setup using environment variables.
Outlines reusable request and response handling patterns.
Demonstrates retry, timeout, and rate limit strategies.
Explains webhook signature verification and event handling.
Provides REST client, pagination, Stripe, SendGrid, and Twilio examples.
Lists troubleshooting checks for authentication, limits, and timeouts.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a tested SDK.
Examples need adaptation for each provider and framework.
It does not validate live API credentials or provider accounts.
Generated code still needs security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Add a payment provider
use_cases.description: Implement Stripe-style payment workflows with authentication, retries, and error handling before launch.

use_cases.title: Build webhook receivers
use_cases.description: Verify signatures and map incoming provider events into internal application actions.

use_cases.title: Improve API reliability
use_cases.description: Add rate limits, pagination, monitoring, and retry behavior to existing integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic API client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new provider integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a REST API client for [service]. Include authentication, request helpers, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add reliable retries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate reliability review for an existing integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my API integration for [service]. Suggest retry, timeout, and rate limit changes that avoid duplicate side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Implement webhook validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced event processing with provider callbacks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a webhook handler for [provider]. Include signature verification, event parsing, idempotency, and safe error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review before production release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this API integration architecture for [service]. Identify risks in authentication, observability, pagination, retries, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: User asks for a REST client for a billing provider.
output: A client structure with configuration, request helpers, resource methods, and error handling.
Notes for API key storage, retries, rate limits, and payment idempotency.

output_examples.input: User asks how to handle webhook events safely.
output_examples.output: A webhook plan with signature verification, raw body parsing, replay protection, event routing, and monitoring checks.

output_examples.input: User asks why API calls fail under load.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering rate limits, timeouts, server errors, retries, pagination, and provider status checks.

best_practices: Keep credentials in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Make retries idempotent and avoid repeating unsafe writes.
Redact tokens, headers, and personal data before logging requests.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding provider keys in source files.
Retrying every error without checking status codes.
Accepting webhook payloads without signature verification.

faq.question: Does this skill make live API calls?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and example patterns unless the user asks an agent to run code.

faq.question: Can it help with OAuth?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers authorization code flows, scopes, redirect URIs, and token exchange concepts.

faq.question: Does it store secrets?
faq.answer: No. It recommends environment variables or secret management, but users must configure storage securely.

faq.question: Which API styles does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers REST APIs, webhooks, pagination, and common third-party SDK patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace provider documentation?
faq.answer: No. Provider-specific limits, fields, and error codes should be checked against official documentation.

faq.question: What should users review before production?
faq.answer: Review secret handling, request signing, webhook verification, retries, idempotency, logging, and monitoring.
